model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between accuracy (ACC, in percent) and co-occurrence number for five different methods: Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," uses a logarithmic scale ranging from $10^1$ to $10^3$, with major tick marks at $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is a linear scale from 0 to 65, with major tick marks at 0, 40, 50, and 60. The data for each method is represented by a distinct line with a corresponding marker and color: Base (black, solid line with circle markers), MEND (brown, solid line with diamond markers), FT (blue, solid line with triangle markers), MEMIT (purple, solid line with circle markers), and ROME (green, solid line with square markers). The ROME method consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 52% at a co-occurrence number of $10^1$ and increasing to over 65% at $10^3$. The MEMIT method shows the second-highest accuracy, starting at about 45% and rising to approximately 55% at $10^3$. The MEND method starts at about 45% and increases to around 56% at $10^3$. The FT method begins at approximately 41% and increases to about 48% at $10^3$. The Base method starts at around 40% and increases to approximately 45% at $10^3$. All methods show a general increasing trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
